summary: St. Joe National Forest site near Calder, Shoshone County: 1930s camp with two patrol points, called abandoned with no date; no source describes what remains.

facts.status_note: Both pages call the site abandoned, with no date. Neither says the structure was removed or describes what remains.

events.note: Camp; pages give only the 1930s, so the year is the decade start

evidence.supports: site in the St. Joe National Forest
about three miles east-northeast of Calder
patrol point one half mile west atop Billy Goat Hill
evidence.quote: 1/2 mile west atop Billy Goat Hill

evidence.supports: patrol point two miles northeast atop O'Neill Hill
Idaho Fire Lookouts also lists the two-mile patrol point atop O'Neill Hill
separate Elk Ridge lookout on the Kaniksu National Forest in Bonner County
the separate Elk Ridge record is in Bonner County

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Idaho Fire Lookouts gives 3320 feet and firelookout.com gives 3220 feet. The story reports both; the record has no elevation key.

corrections.why: Both cited pages say abandoned, with no date. Neither says the site was removed or describes what remains, so 'gone' is not supported by these sources.

notes_for_editor: Thin record: two pages on this tower, no dates beyond the 1930s, no staffing. Do not confuse with the Bonner County Elk Ridge (Kaniksu NF, 54N-3E-10, cited as source 3 and idahofirelookouts cda-region/elk-ridge) or the Nez Perce Elk Ridge (firelookout.com elkridge292, Moose Creek, 1935 camp, abandoned 1942); both are different towers. firelookout.com spells the hill 'Bily Goat Hill'; the story uses Idaho Fire Lookouts' 'Billy Goat Hill'. The O'Neill Hill page on idahofirelookouts describes a separate tower and is not used. The brief's status 'gone' is the only correction proposed; coordinates (47.28799, -116.24831) were not checked.
